paragraphs: A patrol motorcycle is a touring bike loaded with equipment: a windscreen, crash bars, hard panniers, a radio box, emergency lights front and rear and a siren. All of that hardware changes the silhouette so completely that the base motorcycle underneath almost disappears, which is why a plain bike with a light bar never convinces.
The mesh runs 171,993 polygons and 175,379 vertices in quads and tris. The UVs overlap, which is a sound economy on a machine with paired panniers, mirrors and light housings.

At $129 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits law enforcement and urban visualisation, period and contemporary film and television, traffic and road safety material, advertising and games. On sale since 2025.

A scout vehicle is built to see without being seen, and the Fennek shows it: a low flat hull, a very quiet drivetrain and a sensor mast that extends from behind the crew compartment so the vehicle can observe from cover with only the head showing. That mast is the whole point of the design.
The mesh runs 381,217 polygons and 412,910 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 15 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the camouflage, the stencils and the dust.

A rigged build sits on this page at $149. The static model at $129 covers defence and reconnaissance visualisation, news and documentary graphics, training material, film and television, and games. On sale since 2017.

An electric air taxi is defined by its rotors: several of them, distributed along the wing and booms, some tilting for forward flight and some fixed for lift. That distribution is what makes the aircraft safe with a rotor out and what gives the whole eVTOL category its distinctive multi-propeller look.

The mesh is efficient at 61,697 polygons and 67,444 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits an aircraft usually shown in flight over a city or on a vertiport pad rather than in close-up.

This page carries a second static build at $129 and a rigged version at $149 for when the rotors turn or tilt. Aimed at urban air mobility marketing, future transport and smart city visualisation, investor and concept presentation, and games. Built to StemCell specification, on sale since 2025.

A generic pickup earns its keep precisely by not being branded. Architectural renders, advertising that cannot show a competitor's badge, training material and games all need a vehicle that reads as a contemporary crew cab truck without belonging to anyone, and that unbranded quality is the product rather than a compromise.
The mesh runs 368,264 polygons and 423,468 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 4 texture maps at a mix of sizes up to 4096x4096.

This page carries a simple interior build at $99, a simplified grey version at $99 and a rigged build at $149. Aimed at architectural and urban visualisation, advertising, training and safety material, background traffic and games. On sale since 2017.

A panda without vegetation is a bear on a white background. The animal is inseparable in the public imagination from the plant it spends most of its waking hours eating, and a collection that supplies both lets a scene show the behaviour rather than just the species.
Having the animal and the vegetation from one source also keeps the scale honest between them, which is exactly what goes wrong when a creature and its habitat are bought separately.
At $129 it suits wildlife documentary and conservation material, zoo and museum presentation, children's and education content, advertising and games. On sale since 2022.

A raptor is judged on its feathers. The primaries have to overlap in the right order, the coverts have to layer over them, and the whole wing has to look like thousands of separate structures rather than a textured surface. This build carries a genuinely large texture set for that reason: 43 maps at a wide spread of sizes, many of them small and tall because they are individual feathers.

The mesh is 36,376 polygons and 67,816 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout. The vertex count running well above the polygon count is what happens when feather cards and body mesh are combined.
At $129 it suits wildlife documentary and education, conservation and falconry material, advertising, film and television, and games. On sale since 2016.

The egg-shaped fuselage of this light helicopter is one of the most recognisable in aviation, and it came from a military requirement for a small observation aircraft. In police colours the same airframe becomes the machine that circles a city at night with a searchlight and a camera turret, and this build carries that equipment.

The texture load is exceptional for a helicopter this size: 79 maps in total, with 6 at 8192x8192, 4 at 6144x6144, 7 at 4096x4096, 57 at 2048x2048 and 5 at 1024x1024, on a mesh of 253,230 polygons and 261,403 vertices with non-overlapping UVs.

A rigged build sits on this page at $149. The static model at $129 covers law enforcement and emergency services visualisation, urban night scenes, film and television, documentary work and games. On sale since 2016.

A traditional pub bar is a piece of joinery as much as furniture: a heavy timber counter, turned columns, an arched glass rack overhead and a bank of taps along the top. The arch is the feature that reads first across a room, and it is what separates a pub from a modern bar with a straight run of shelving.

The mesh runs 511,032 polygons and 522,488 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, with the density in the mouldings, the turned detail and the tap assemblies where a camera at the counter lands.

At $129 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits hospitality and interior visualisation, pub and restaurant design presentation, film and television set dressing, brewery marketing and games. On sale since 2026.

The R22 is the helicopter most civilian pilots learn on, and it is tiny: two seats, a teetering two-blade rotor, skids and a slim tail boom, with a control system that uses a shared T-bar cyclic rising between the seats. That T-bar is one of the details a pilot looks for immediately.

The mesh runs 230,562 polygons and 243,228 vertices in quads and tris. The UVs overlap, which is a sound economy on a small symmetrical airframe, and the CheckMate build keeps the surfacing clean enough for close inspection.
At $129 it suits flight training and general aviation visualisation, helicopter school marketing, airfield and heliport scenes, film and television, and games. On sale since 2026.

A rotary parlour is an assembly line for milking: cows step onto a slowly turning platform, are attached at one point and step off a full revolution later. Modelling it properly means the platform, the stalls, the cluster arms, the pipework overhead and the barn around it all have to be there, along with the animals themselves.

It is a large asset at 2,743,592 polygons and 2,908,966 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and it includes fur grooming on the cattle, which is what stops the animals reading as plastic in an otherwise industrial scene.

At $129 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits dairy and agritech visualisation, farming industry presentation, food supply chain material, education and documentary work, and games. On sale since 2025.

This tower sits on its own island in the bay, and its form is unusual: a slab that splits into two towers above the podium and rejoins at the top, leaving a rectangular void through the middle of the building. That opening is the whole architectural signature, and it is visible from every angle of the city.
The mesh runs 608,061 polygons and 642,604 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density in the facade module and the crown structure that spans the towers.

At $119 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits architectural and city visualisation, hospitality and property marketing, tourism material, film and television establishing shots, and games. On sale since 2026.

This loitering munition is a delta wing with a pusher propeller and no landing gear at all, because it is not meant to come back. It launches from a rail in batches, cruises on a small engine and flies into its target. The simplicity is deliberate: the airframe exists to be cheap enough to use in numbers.
The mesh is 250,486 polygons and 127,145 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the wing planform, the engine mount and the launch rail fittings.

A rigged build sits on this page at the same $119. Both suit defence and geopolitical visualisation, news and documentary graphics, strategic analysis material, training and games. Built to StemCell specification, on sale since 2023.

A light twin in corporate livery is a very specific object: the same airframe that does police, medical and utility work, but finished in gloss with a company scheme and no external equipment. That cleanliness is what makes it useful for marketing imagery, where sensors and winches would clutter the shape.

The mesh is heavy for its size at 1,036,212 polygons and 1,064,988 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 19 texture maps at 4096x4096. That density shows in the rotor head and the door frames.
A rigged build sits on this page at $169. The static model at $119 covers corporate aviation marketing, charter and utility operator presentation, film and television, and games. On sale since 2017.

A terminal tractor exists to shuffle trailers around a yard, and everything about it follows from that: a very short wheelbase for turning in tight spaces, a lifting fifth wheel so the driver never has to wind legs up and down, a single cab door for quick exits and no need for high speed at all.

The mesh runs 445,660 polygons and 439,473 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 14 texture maps - 11 at 4096x4096 and 3 at 2048x2048 carrying the paint, the safety markings and the yard grime.

A rigged build sits on this page at $139. The static model at $119 covers logistics and warehouse visualisation, port and terminal scenes, equipment marketing, supply chain presentation and games. On sale since 2019.
